description: A nine-panel composite figure combining TEM bright-field (BF) and dark-field (DF) micrographs, one SAED pattern and one XRD pattern, used to identify bainite (B), tempered martensite (TM), ferrite (F), fresh martensite (FM) and retained austenite (RA) in three tempered low-density steels. (a) BF TEM of AN750-T, 1 µm scale bar, with regions labelled TM, F and B. (b) BF/DF pair of B, 200 nm scale bar. (c) BF/DF pair of RA, 100 nm scale bar, one field labelled FM. (d) SAED of RA, 10 1/nm scale bar, indexed along [110]γ and showing 002γ, 111γ and 1̄11γ reflections. (e) BF TEM of AN800-T, 1 µm, labelled TM and B. (f) 200 nm BF image contrasting carbide distribution in B and TM (F, TM, B labelled). (g) XRD after tempering: three vertically stacked patterns, AN850-T (blue, top), AN800-T (red, middle) and AN750-T (black, bottom), over 2θ = 30-100°, with peaks indexed α(110), γ(200), α(200), γ(220), α(211), γ(311), α(220). (h) BF TEM of AN850-T, 2 µm. (i) BF and DF images of B and TM, 1 µm. The figure links carbide orientation to B/TM discrimination and shows weakening γ (RA) reflections from AN750-T to AN850-T.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field micrograph of AN750-T with a 1 µm scale bar; regions labelled TM, F and B in a mixed lath plus equiaxed morphology.
Bright-field and dark-field image pair of bainite (B), 200 nm scale bar; the dark-field frame shows bright laths of bainite on a dark background.
Bright-field and dark-field image pair of retained austenite (RA), 100 nm scale bar; one field labelled FM, with RA appearing as a bright thin band in the dark-field image.
Selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of RA, scale bar 10 1/nm, marked [110]γ, with indexed spots 002γ, 111γ, 1̄11γ, 1̄1̄1γ, 11̄1γ.
TEM bright-field micrograph of AN800-T, 1 µm scale bar, with areas labelled TM and B.
TEM micrograph at 200 nm scale bar comparing carbide appearance/distribution in bainite and tempered martensite; regions labelled F, TM and B.

X-ray diffraction patterns after tempering, three vertically offset traces labelled AN850-T (blue, top), AN800-T (red, middle) and AN750-T (black, bottom), x-axis 2θ (°) from 30 to 100, y-axis Intensity (a.u.).
TEM bright-field micrograph of AN850-T, 2 µm scale bar, showing a region labelled F and a lath/block structure.
Bright-field and dark-field TEM image pair of B and TM, 1 µm scale bar; the dark-field frame highlights the lath substructure.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM bright-field micrograph of AN750-T with a 1 µm scale bar and areas labelled TM, F and B.
Panel (d) is an SAED pattern of retained austenite with a 10 1/nm scale bar, indexed along the [110]γ zone axis and showing 002γ, 111γ and 1̄11γ reflections.
Panel (g) plots XRD intensity (a.u.) against 2θ (°) from 30 to 100 with three vertically stacked traces for AN850-T (blue, top), AN800-T (red, middle) and AN750-T (black, bottom).
Panel (g) labels the indexed reflections α(110), γ(200), α(200), γ(220), α(211), γ(311) and α(220), so both BCC α and FCC γ (austenite) reflections are indexed in all three tempered conditions.
The SAED pattern in (d) is a single-crystal-type spot pattern along [110]γ, consistent with the presence of austenite phase, not a polycrystalline ring pattern.

Panels (b), (c) and (i) each pair a bright-field with a dark-field image; the dark-field frames show the bainitic/RA features as bright bands on a dark background, scale bars 200 nm, 100 nm and 1 µm respectively.
The figure is a composite containing TEM bright-field/dark-field micrographs with scale bars of 2 µm, 1 µm, 200 nm and 100 nm, an SAED pattern (10 1/nm) and an XRD plot.
The caption states the figure is 'Identification of B and TM based on TEM and discovery of RA', with (h) AN850-T and (i) bright-field and dark-field images of B and TM.

Citing text states that bainite carbides lie at about a 60° angle to the bainitic ferrite boundaries, whereas tempered martensite carbides are randomly distributed, and that this difference in orientation distinguishes bainite from tempered martensite (Fig. 4).
Citing text states EBSD struggles to distinguish bainite from tempered martensite because of their similar mechanical properties, so the two are grouped as B/TM.
Citing text gives retained austenite contents of 7.4%, 2.4% and 0.6% for AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T respectively; these numbers are not printed in Fig. 4 itself.

unreadable_items: panel (f): individual carbides in B and TM are not clearly resolvable at the supplied resolution; the ~60° carbide-to-boundary angle asserted in the text cannot be measured from the pixels
panels (b), (c), (i): the bright-field and dark-field frame pairs are low-contrast and the internal lath/RA detail is only partially readable
panel (g): relative γ-peak intensities (e.g. γ(220) vs α(211)) cannot be read quantitatively because no intensity scale or numeric labels are printed
